title: Proactive Telemetry Sentinel for early billing & latency outlier detection
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight backend service (Telemetry Sentinel) that produces early-warning alerts for billing/cost drift and incipient latency degradations across customer cohorts and infra/region/model dimensions. Unlike the current spike detectors, Sentinel emphasizes fast detection of gradual drifts, correlated multi-metric anomalies, and high-precision customer-level alerts to reduce noisy pages and actionable investigation work.

Scope:
- Real-time stream ingestion of pre-aggregated usage records (per-customer, per-region, per-model, per-route) from the existing Kafka topic.
- A two-layer detection pipeline: (1) fast statistical detectors for low-latency signals (EWMA, change-point on rolling quantiles, short-window rate-of-change) and (2) a heavier correlation/verification pass (isolation-forest / lightweight gradient boosting on derived features + cross-metric correlation scoring) that runs on a sliding window.
- Confidence scoring + deduplication and adaptive suppression windows to avoid duplicate alerts across related dimensions.
- RCA hints in the alert payload: correlated metrics (cost vs token-rate, latency vs queue-depth), model/version tags, recent rollout flags.
- Integrate with Console alert inbox + external sinks (Slack channels, PagerDuty) and attach links to timelines and quick links to the Live Metrics view.

Why this is different: existing detectors focus on point spikes or per-metric thresholds. Sentinel is designed for:
- Early detection of slow cost drift (e.g., quantization/rollout regressions or tokenization changes) that can manifest over hours/days.
- Correlated anomalies where cost and latency move together due to autoscaler misconfig, kernel fallback, or serving-node saturation.
- High-precision customer-level alerts that include contextual evidence to make on-call triage faster.

Success metrics:
- Reduce false-positive alert rate for customer-level cost/latency alerts by >= 50% vs current baseline.
- Median detection latency <= 10 minutes for fast signals, <= 60 minutes for drift detections.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for high-confidence customer-impact alerts <= 30 minutes in pilot orgs.

Non-goals: automatic remediation, full ML model retraining infra, replacing existing Spike Detector microservice (we will interoperate).

Architecture notes:
- Ingest: Kafka topic "telemetry.aggregates.v2" (hourly and 1m windows).
- Fast path: Flink (or Beam) job with lightweight detectors that emits candidate events to a verification topic.
- Verify path: a horizontally-scalable worker pool (Kubernetes) that loads small feature windows from ClickHouse and runs the correlation model and produces a confidence score.
- Storage: ClickHouse for feature windows / historical baselines; S3 for serialized detector artifacts.
- Alerting: write canonical alerts to Alertstore (existing schema) then route to console/pager/integrations.

Privacy/Cost trade-offs: to keep costs bounded we will operate primarily on aggregated keys and avoid raw request payloads. Customer-level detection will be enabled via sampling and rate-limited evaluation in the heavy path.

Deliverables:
- Prototype fast-path Flink job and verification worker (PoC integrated with a test Kafka topic).
- Console inbox integration + alert payload schema updates.
- Dashboards: detection throughput, false-positive rate, detection latency, top contributing features for flagged alerts.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Final choice between Flink and Managed Beam (GCP) for streaming. (ENG infra + cost input needed)
- Whether to persist intermediate candidate events for offline audits (privacy/cost trade-off).
- Default suppression logic: fixed windows vs adaptive based on metric volatility.

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.local/display/CONSOLE/Telemetry+Sentinel+Design (WIP)
- Proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/198

acceptance_criteria: Fast-path emits candidate events for 99% of injected synthetic anomalies in staging
Verification pass assigns confidence score and the pipeline deduplicates related alerts before writing to Alertstore
Console displays generated alerts with RCA hints and links to Live Metrics timeline
False positive rate for pilot customers reduced by >= 40% compared to baseline (measured over 2 weeks)
implementation_notes: Keep detectors pluggable: implement interface so new detectors can be added without altering pipeline wiring
Ship with feature-flag gating for customer-level verification to control sampling and rollout
Emit detailed detector telemetry (reason codes, contributing features) at INFO-level to a separate metrics stream for offline model improvement
Use a low-memory isolation forest implementation (scikit-learn lofi or custom) to keep verification worker footprint small
rollout_plan: Week 1: PoC fast-path + verification worker in internal staging; smoke tests with synthetic anomalies
Week 2: Pilot with 5 beta orgs, sampling customer-level verification at 20%
Week 3-4: Expand to 25% of customers, monitor false-positive rate and detection latency; tune suppression windows
Week 5: Full rollout to all hosted accounts behind feature flag; monitor for 2 weeks before feature-flag removal
